source_text: σοῦν θυμιατήριον, λυχνία τε αὖ καὶ τὰ σκεύη τὰ λειτουργικὰ, τὸ ἄνωθεν ἡμῖν καὶ ἐξ οὐρανοῦ σημαίνοντος τοῦ ὑακινθίνου. Τοιουτόχρως γὰρ ὁ ἄνωθεν καὶ εἰς βάθος αἰθήρ. Ὅτι δὲ τύποι Χριστοῦ τοῦ ἄνωθεν καὶ ἐξ οὐρανοῦ τὰ σκεύη τὰ ἱερὰ, διὰ μακρῶν ἡμῖν ἤδη προαποδέδεικται λόγων. Ἡ δὲ τράπεζα, καὶ ἱμάτιον ὁλοπόρφυρον πρὸς τοῖς ὑακινθίνοις περιβλήμασιν ἔχει· τὸ δέ γε τῶν καρπωμάτων θυσιαστήριον, ἱμάτιον κόκκινον, καὶ μέντοι καὶ ὁ λουτὴρ, ἱμάτιον ὁλοπόρφυρον ἐπὶ πυκάσμασι τοῖς ὑακινθίνοις. Καὶ σημαίνει μὲν ἡ τράπεζα, τὴν πρόθεσιν ἔχουσα τῶν ἄρτων, τὴν ἀναίμακτον θυσίαν, δι' ἧς εὐλογούμεθα τὸν ἄρτον ἐσθίοντες τὸν ἐξ οὐρανοῦ, τοῦτ' ἔστι Χριστὸν, ὃς καὶ γέγονε καθ' ἡμᾶς, ἀλλ' ἦν τε καὶ ἔστι καὶ οὕτως Θεὸς ἄνωθέν τε καὶ ἐκ Πατρὸς ἐρχόμενος, καὶ ἐπάνω πάντων ὡς τῶν ὅλων βασιλεὺς καὶ Κύριος. Αἴνιγμα δὲ τῆς τοῦ Χριστοῦ βασιλείας εἴη ἂν, ὡς ἔμοιγε φαίνεται, τὸ ἐπιτετανύσθαι τῇ τραπέζῃ τὸ ἁλουργὲς ἱμάτιον, ἤτοι τὸ περίβλημα τὸ πορφυροῦν. Κατημφίεστο δὲ τόδε τῶν καρπωμάτων θυσιαστήριον ἱματίῳ κοκκίνῳ· ἱμάτιον δὲ τὸ κοκκινοβαφὲς, αἵματος τύπον παραδεξόμεθα. Τέθυται γὰρ δι' ἡμᾶς καὶ ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν ὁ Χριστὸς, καὶ ἀμνὸς οἷά τις ἐπὶ τὸ θεῖον ἀνέβη θυσιαστήριον, εἰς ὀσμὴν εὐωδίας τῷ Θεῷ καὶ Πατρί. Πρὸς δὲ τοῖς ὑακινθίνοις, ἱμάτιον ὁλοπόρφυρον τῷ λουτῆρι τὸ πέτασμα. Γράφει δὲ ὁ λουτὴρ ἐφ' ἑαυτῷ τὸν τύπον τοῦ ἁγίου βαπτίσματος, ὕδασιν ἡμᾶς ἁγίοις ἀπολούοντος εἰς ἀπόθεσιν ἁμαρτίας, καὶ εἰς τὴν τῶν οὐρανῶν βασιλείαν ἀποκομίζοντος. Ἄνωθεν δὲ καὶ ἐξ οὐρανοῦ τὸ ἅγιον βάπτισμα· αἴνιγμα δὲ τούτου, τὸ χρῶμα τὸ ὑακίνθινον. Ἢ οὐκ ἄριστά σοι ταυτὶ δὴ φάναι δοκῶ, ὡς ἔν γε τοιαύτῃ δυσκαταληψίᾳ θεωρημάτων; {ΠΑΛΛ.} Καὶ μάλα. {ΚΥΡ.} Λειτουργία μὲν οὖν ἡ τοιάδε τοῖς ἀπὸ Καάθ· Γεδσωνῖται δὲ αὖ καὶ μέν τοι καὶ Μεραρῖται, κατὰ τὸν ἴσον τρόπον, ἀπεγράφοντο μὲν ἀπὸ εἴκοσι καὶ πέντε ἐτῶν καὶ μέχρι πεντήκοντα, ὀνομαστὶ δὲ κατ' οἴκους καὶ πατριάς· καὶ λειτουργία μὲν τῷ δήμῳ Γεδσὼν, αἱ δέῤῥεις τῆς σκηνῆς, τὰ καλύμματα, τὰ περιτανύσματα τῶν θυρῶν, καὶ τὰ ἱστία τῆς αὐλῆς καὶ τὰ περισσά· γέγραπται δὲ ὡδί. Τό γε μὴν ἐκ Μεραρὶ (δῆμος δὲ καὶ οὗτος Λευϊτικὸς), οἱ στύλοι τῆς σκηνῆς, αἱ βάσεις, αἱ κεφαλίδες, πάσσαλοί τε καὶ μοχλοὶ, καὶ τὸ καταπέτασμα τῆς σκηνῆς τῆς ἔξω, καὶ ἅττα τινὰ πρὸς τούτοις ἕτερα. Καὶ οἱ μὲν ἀπὸ Γεδσών τε καὶ Μεραρὶ, ταῖς δι' ἁμαξῶν ὑπουργίαις τὰ σφίσιν αὐτοῖς ἐγκεχειρισμένα διεκόμιζον πανταχῆ. Κααθῖταί γε μὴν, τὰ Ἅγια τῶν ἁγίων εἰς ὤμους ἔχοντες ᾔεσαν. Γέγραπται γὰρ οὕτως ἐν τοῖς Ἀριθμοῖς· «Καὶ προσήνεγκαν οἱ ἄρχοντες Ἰσραὴλ δώδεκα ἄρχοντες οἴκων πατριῶν αὐτῶν· οὗτοι οἱ ἄρχοντες φυλῶν, οὗτοι οἱ παρεστηκότες ἐπὶ τῆς ἐπισκοπῆς, καὶ ἤνεγκαν τὰ δῶρα αὐτῶν ἔναντι Κυρίου, ἓξ ἁμάξας λαμπηνίκας καὶ δώδεκα βόας. Ἅμαξαν παρὰ δύο ἀρχόντων,
pass_a_gloss: [from §5: the golden] incense altar, lampstand again and the vessels of service, the hyacinth/blue signifying to us the 'from above' and 'from heaven'. For of such colour is the upper and deep reaching aether/upper air. And that the sacred vessels are types of Christ who is from above and from heaven, has already been shown beforehand through long discourses. The table has an all purple cloth in addition to the blue wrappings; the altar of whole burnt offerings a scarlet cloth; and the laver an all purple cloth over the blue coverings. And the table, having the setting forth of the loaves, signifies the bloodless sacrifice, through which we are blessed eating the bread from heaven, that is Christ, who also became according to us, but was and is even so God, coming from above and from the Father, and above all as king and Lord of the whole. An enigma/riddle of Christ's kingdom/kingship would be, as it seems to me, the sea purple cloth's being stretched over the table, i.e. the purple wrapping. And the altar of whole burnt offerings was clothed in a scarlet cloth; the scarlet dyed cloth we shall accept as a type of blood. For Christ has been sacrificed on account of us and on behalf of us, and like some lamb went up onto the divine altar, unto an odour of sweet smell to the God and Father. In addition to the blue, an all purple cloth [is] the spread cover for the laver. The laver writes on itself the type of holy baptism, washing us off with holy waters unto putting away of sin, and carrying off into the kingdom of the heavens. And holy baptism is from above and from heaven; an enigma of this, the blue colour. Or do I not seem to you to say these things excellently, as in such difficulty of grasping of contemplations? PALL.: Very much. CYR.: Such then the service for those from Kohath; and Gershonites again and also Merarites, in the equal manner, were enrolled from 25 years and up to 50, by name, by houses and paternal families; and service for the clan of Gershon: the hide curtains of the tent, the coverings, the hangings around of the doors, and the sails/hangings of the court, and the extra things; it is written so. And that from Merari (this too a Levitical clan): the pillars of the tent, the bases, the capitals, pegs and bars, and the veil of the outer tent, and some other things besides. And those from Gershon and Merari conveyed everywhere the things entrusted to them by services through wagons; but Kohathites went having the holy of holies on shoulders. For it is written thus in Numbers: 'And the rulers of Israel brought, twelve rulers of houses of their families; these the rulers of tribes, these those standing over the inspection/census, and they brought their gifts before the Lord, six covered wagons and twelve oxen, a wagon from two rulers, [continued §7]
pass_b_english: Cyril: …the blue signifying for us what is from above and from heaven. For that is the color of the upper air, high and deep above us. That the sacred vessels are types of Christ, who is from above and from heaven, we have already shown at length. The table, besides its blue wrappings, also has a cloth of pure purple; the altar of burnt offerings has a scarlet cloth; and the laver too has a cloth of pure purple over its blue coverings. The table, on which the loaves are set out, signifies the bloodless sacrifice, through which we are blessed as we eat the bread from heaven (John 6:51), that is, Christ. He became as we are, yet even so he was and is God, coming from above and from the Father, and above all things (John 3:31), as King and Lord of the universe. And the royal purple cloth spread over the table, that is, the purple wrapping, would be, as it seems to me, a sign of Christ’s kingship. The altar of burnt offerings was clothed in a scarlet cloth, and we shall take the cloth dyed scarlet as a type of blood. For Christ was sacrificed for our sake and on our behalf (1 Corinthians 5:7), and like a lamb he went up onto the divine altar, as a fragrant offering to God the Father (Ephesians 5:2). The laver’s covering, besides the blue, is a cloth of pure purple. The laver bears in itself the type of holy baptism, which washes us in holy waters for the putting away of sin and carries us into the kingdom of heaven. Holy baptism is from above and from heaven, and the blue color hints at this. Or do I not seem to you to have explained these things very well, given how hard such insights are to grasp?

Cyril: Such, then, was the service of those from Kohath. The Gershonites, and the Merarites as well, were enrolled in the same way, from twenty-five years old up to fifty, by name, by households and families (Numbers 4:22–23, 29–30). The service of the clan of Gershon was the hide curtains of the tent, the coverings, the screens of the doors, the hangings of the court, and the extra things (Numbers 4:24–26). So it is written. To the clan of Merari (this too is a Levitical clan) belonged the pillars of the tent, the bases, the capitals, the pegs and bars, the veil of the outer tent, and certain other things besides (Numbers 4:31–32). Those from Gershon and Merari carried the things entrusted to them from place to place with the help of wagons, but the Kohathites went with the most holy things on their shoulders. For it is written in Numbers: ‘The rulers of Israel brought offerings, twelve rulers of their fathers’ houses. These were the rulers of the tribes; these were the men who stood over the census. They brought their gifts before the Lord, six covered wagons and twelve oxen, a wagon from every two rulers…’ (Numbers 7:2–3)

choices.why: λαμπηνικός rendered 'covered' (LXX λαμπήνη, a covered wagon).

anf_compare.notes: No public-domain English of De adoratione Book 13 to compare. Sense taken from the PG 68 Greek. The withheld earlier English was not used as a model.

apparatus.note: PG 68.853. Opens mid-word (χρυ|σοῦν θυμιατήριον) completing the last sentence of §5; the English begins with an ellipsis after the comma. θυμιατήριον here names the golden altar (Numbers 4:11, 'the golden altar'), rendered 'golden altar of incense' in §5. Discrepancy in Cyril, kept as written: in the quotation (Numbers 4:8, 4:13) the scarlet cloth goes over the table's vessels and the all-purple cloth over the altar of burnt offering, but here Cyril assigns scarlet to the altar of burnt offerings and purple to the table; his allegory follows his own assignment. He calls the laver's cloth 'all-purple' (ὁλοπόρφυρον) though the quoted LXX plus in 4:14 says 'purple' (πορφυροῦν). 'The bread from heaven' that is eaten: John 6:50-51 (cited 6:51). 'Coming from above ... above all' echoes John 3:31 (ὁ ἄνωθεν ἐρχόμενος ἐπάνω πάντων ἐστίν). 'Sacrificed for us' follows 1 Corinthians 5:7 (ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν ἐτύθη Χριστός, as in the Byzantine text); 'a fragrant offering to God' follows Ephesians 5:2 (εἰς ὀσμὴν εὐωδίας). 'Like a lamb' may recall Isaiah 53:7 or John 1:29, but the image of going up on the altar matches neither; no citation. 'Washes us ... for the putting away of sin' may recall Acts 22:16 or 1 Peter 3:21 (ἀπόθεσις); not certain, no citation. 'Baptism is from above' may recall John 3:3, 5 (γεννηθῆναι ἄνωθεν); not certain, no citation. Gershon and Merari: Cyril paraphrases Numbers 4:22-33 (LXX gives twenty-five years, Hebrew thirty). 'The extra things' renders τὰ περισσά, the LXX phrase in Numbers 4:26, which Cyril interprets in §7. γέγραπται δὲ ὡδί ('so it is written') is followed by no quotation in PG; Cyril either points back to the paraphrase or a quotation has dropped out. The Merari list (including 'the veil of the outer tent') is Cyril's own summary and does not match Numbers 4:31-32 item for item. The quotation of Numbers 7:2-9 is split across §6 and §7 (break after 'a wagon from every two rulers'). λαμπηνικός rendered 'covered' (LXX λαμπήνη, a covered wagon).
